quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes safely and let them go ahead. Speeding up may make things more dangerous.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Which item provides the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield does not offer enough protection.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It does not mean they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not count on eye contact to guarantee that a driver will yield. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but fail to notice them.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Riders should be extra careful at intersections.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Why should you look over your shoulder before changing lanes on a motorcycle?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
You should make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you are riding right next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay next to them until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or slow down to move away from alongside the vehicle.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals can show turns or stops. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider will turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: Which item protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from the wind. Windshields, sunglasses, and eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is strapped on securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is strapped on securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is strapped on securely is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of crashing, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, use your turn signals, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: Penalties for drinking and riding are:

options.text: Up to a judge to decide.

questions.explanation: Oregon law has strict penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Riding between two vehicles moving in the same direction:

options.text: Is allowed when traffic is heavy.
Is allowed during the day to reduce traffic.
Is okay if you feel comfortable doing it.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, it is illegal for motorcycles to pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: If you shift to a lower gear without going slowly enough, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could jerk forward and the rear tire could slide.
Motorcycle could speed up too fast.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could jerk forward and the rear tire could slide.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear without riding slowly enough, the motorcycle will jerk forward and the rear tire may slide.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop faster.
Brake lighter than usual to protect your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more distance to stop completely.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually located:
questions.explanation: The rear brake of a motorcycle is operated with the right foot.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hand ready on the clutch and both brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hand ready on the clutch and both brakes.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hand ready on the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT do when riding at night for safety?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.explanation: Ride safely at night by reducing your speed, using your high beam headlight when not near other vehicles, and increasing your following distance. Watch the headlights and taillights of vehicles ahead to help you see the road.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.
Happen because passengers distract the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who have less than six months of experience on that particular motorcycle. Always be very careful when riding a motorcycle that is new to you.

questions.question: When merging onto a highway, a group of riders should form a:
questions.explanation: Riders should use a single-file line when entering or exiting a highway, turning, or riding curves. A staggered line is better for normal riding on straight roads.

questions.question: What sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for at least one hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long, usually within a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in the driver's blind spot. The driver may change lanes without seeing you. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Travel slower than you would during the day.
Travel at the same speed as during the day.
Travel faster than you would during the day.
Ride on the road shoulder so other vehicles see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Travel slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding at night. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Riding slower helps you avoid dangers and gives you more time to react.
